fatal_errors: The material is incorrectly treated as a homogeneous single-phase HEA; the target is as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 with FCC and B2 phases.
The governing intervention is missed: intermediate-temperature thermal aging, especially at approximately 600°C and 750°C, rather than high-rate or cyclic loading itself.
The proposed monotonic loading-induced embrittlement does not reconstruct the observed ductile-brittle-ductile dependence on aging temperature.
The mechanism omits enhanced L12 ordering, increased APBE and modulus, restricted cross-slip, jagged B2/FCC phase boundaries, and crack initiation at phase-boundary tips.
The stated evidence does not establish mechanically induced segregation or precipitation as a cause of brittle fracture; some cited evidence instead reports SRO destruction or retained ductility.
explanation: The response addresses toughness degradation in HEAs and gives a nominally controlled loaded-versus-unloaded comparison with a falsification rule, but it does not recover the target material, treatment, temperature window, mechanism, or non-monotonic outcome. The target behavior is aging-controlled: maximal L12 ordering and jagged FCC/B2 boundary density near 600°C promote planar slip, pile-ups, stress concentration, and embrittlement, while reduced ordering and ductile transition zones near 750°C restore ductility. The proposed service boundaries are vague and omit the <550°C, 550–750°C, and >750°C regimes. Its experiment could test its own hypothesis, although a preloaded-versus-unloaded comparison also risks conflating accumulated damage with microstructural causation. Evidence E1 concerns thermally aged TiVNbTa and softening, E3 reports deformation-induced destruction of SRO, and E4–E5 show phase-separated material retaining ductile fracture; thus the citations do not support the claimed causal chain.
